title: The compiler relies on the Rules of React

slides.text: The compiler trusts you to follow the rules 📏
slides.say: React Compiler is stable and used in production. But it makes one big assumption about your code.

slides.text: It's built for code that follows the Rules of React. If it sees code that might break them, it skips optimizing it instead of risking a change in behavior.
slides.say: It's designed for code that follows the rules of React. When it spots code that might break them, it safely skips that code instead of changing how your app behaves.

slides.text: The danger: violations it can't detect. Then it compiles code it should have skipped, and you get runtime bugs.
slides.say: The real danger is a violation it can't detect. Then it compiles a component it should have skipped, and you get bugs at runtime.
A common cause is code that relies on memoization for correctness. Here the effect only re-runs because filters is a new object each render. After compiling, it may fire differently.

slides.text: Fix the Rules of React violations the ESLint plugin reports. A healthy codebase makes the rollout safe.
slides.say: So fix the rules of React violations that the ESLint plugin reports. How safe your rollout is depends on how well your code follows the rules.
